title: Independent critique of a candidate model breakdown
description: Written by a critique LLM that did NOT produce the candidate. The critic files issues; it never edits analysis_config.json. Its authority is evidence: every issue must cite source, config or trace locators a deterministic script can re-check, which is what separates a critique from an opinion.

critique_kind.description: Optional for legacy reports. New formal reports identify themselves as the full final eleven-item critique.

status.description: `failed` whenever any issue has severity `error`. `unknown` means the critic could not reach a verdict (evidence absent), which never counts as passing.

critic.description: Identifier for the critiquing agent/model. Recorded so a critique produced by the same context that produced the candidate is visible rather than implicit.

artifacts.description: SHA256 of every input the critique was formed against. Any drift invalidates this report: a critique of bytes that no longer exist proves nothing about the bytes that do.

dataflow_source.description: Optional only because a source-less run has no dataflow truth to bind. Whenever the runner supplies one, validate_critique.py requires it here.

checkpoint_config.description: The checkpoint's own config.json. Distinct from Python defaults read out of modeling source -- binding this is what lifts evidence_cap to 100.

source_index.description: Deterministic source index bound to the source bundle used by the critic.

raw_ops_compact.description: Compact raw-op evidence actually exposed to the final critic.

source_snippets.description: Indexed source snippets actually exposed to the final critic.

context_manifest.description: The final clean-context input whitelist used by the critic.

checks.description: One entry per mandatory critique dimension. All eleven must appear; a dimension the critic could not judge is `unknown`, never omitted.

issues.description: Empty only when the critic found nothing. Each issue is a falsifiable claim about the candidate, not a style note.

issue_ids.description: Issues filed under this check. A `failed` check must name at least one.

evidence.description: At least one locator (source_ref, config_path or op_indices) must accompany the explanation, so the claim can be re-checked mechanically rather than believed.

issue.description: claim/expected/observed are separate fields on purpose: an issue that cannot state what the candidate asserted, what the evidence requires, and what was actually found is not yet a finding.

severity.description: `error` blocks. `warning` and `info` do not block by themselves but are reported.

observed.description: What was actually found in source/config/trace.

source_evidence.description: `modeling.py:123` style refs that must resolve to real lines.

trace_evidence.description: op indices in the representative step.

repair.description: Direction only. The critic states what is wrong and where to look, never a ready-made replacement config -- handing over the answer would make the next round a transcription rather than a decomposition.

check_id.description: Which mandatory check this issue was filed under.
